Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (a dashboard that shows data, anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.text:
## VSCode'da EVREN: üç yol

Önce **tek seferlik şartlar onayı** gerekir, yoksa her istemci 403 `terms_not_accepted` alır. PowerShell'de anahtarınızla bir kez çalıştırın:

```powershell
$env:EVREN_API_KEY = "evren_llm_..."
$h = @{ "X-API-Key" = $env:EVREN_API_KEY }
$v = (Invoke-RestMethod "https://evren-llmapi.ssyz.org.tr/v1/terms/status" -Headers $h).current_version
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post "https://evren-llmapi.ssyz.org.tr/v1/terms/accept" -Headers $h `
  -ContentType "application/json" -Body (@{ version = $v } | ConvertTo-Json)
Invoke-RestMethod "https://evren-llmapi.ssyz.org.tr/v1/quota" -Headers $h   # kota kontrolü
```

### 1. Continue (hazır — sadece anahtar lazım)
[config.yaml](~/.continue/config.yaml) dosyanızı doldurdum (eskisi `config.yaml.bak` olarak duruyor). 4 sohbet modeli + `@codebase` için embedding ve reranker tanımlı. Tek yapmanız gereken 6 yerdeki `BURAYA_EVREN_ANAHTARINIZ` metnini anahtarınızla değiştirmek:

```powershell
(Get-Content $HOME\.continue\config.yaml) -replace 'BURAYA_EVREN_ANAHTARINIZ','evren_llm_...' |
  Set-Content $HOME\.continue\config.yaml -Encoding utf8
```

Sonra VSCode'da Continue panelini kapatıp açın; model seçicide "GLM 5.3 (EVREN)" görünür. `provider: openai` + `apiBase` kombinasyonu EVREN'in OpenAI sözleşmesiyle birebir çalışır.

**Not:** satır-içi otomatik tamamlama (autocomplete) rolünü bilinçli olarak eklemedim — o FIM (fill-in-the-middle) formatı ister, filodaki sohbet modelleri bunu `/v1/completions` üzerinden sunmuyor. Tamamlama için Copilot'u ya da yerel bir modeli bırakın.

### 2. Kilo Code (ajan işleri için en iyisi)
Kurulu ve zaten OpenAI-uyumlu sağlayıcı destekliyor; UI'dan 30 saniye:

- Kilo Code panel → ⚙ Settings → Providers → **API Provider: OpenAI Compatible**
- Base URL: `https://evren-llmapi.ssyz.org.tr/v1`
- API Key: anahtarınız
- Model ID: `mimo-v2.6-pro` (Terminal-Bench 89,9 ve 1M bağlam ile ajan döngüsünde en güçlüsü) veya `deepseek-v4.1-flash`
- Model yetenekleri bölümünde: Context Window `1000000`, Max Output Tokens `8192`, Image Support açık

### 3. opencode / Codex
opencode için `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`'a `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` sağlayıcısı eklenir; Codex CLI ise EVREN `/v1/responses` ucunu desteklediği için `OPENAI_BASE_URL` ile doğrudan çalışır. İsterseniz ikisinin dosyalarını da yazayım.

### Dikkat edilecek iki şey
- `max_tokens` düşünme token'larını da kapsıyor, bu yüzden config'de hiçbir modele 2048'in altını vermedim. Hız isterseniz anahtar sayfasından "Düşünme modu"nu kapatın (Continue ve Kilo `thinking: false` göndermiyor).
- Anahtarı bu depodaki (`portable_agent_kit`) hiçbir dosyaya yazmayın — yazdığım config kullanıcı profilinizde, repo dışında; PRINCIPLE-019 gereği izlenen dosyalarda kimlik bilgisi sıfır olmalı.

content.text:
Sebep belli: anahtar hiç girilmemiş. Config'deki 6 satır hâlâ `BURAYA_EVREN_ANAHTARINIZ` yazıyor, yani Continue bu metni gerçek anahtar sanıp geçide gönderiyor ve 401 alıyor. Yapılandırmada başka bir hata yok (YAML temiz, BOM yok).

Anahtarı sohbete yazmanıza gerek yok — sizden isteyip hem şartları onaylayan hem config'i yamalayan bir betik hazırladım:

input.command:
cat > "C:/Users/YUNUS-~1/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-Yunus-Emre-Desktop-portable-agent-kit/139bf0fc-ef11-4922-a268-d5078cb740b4/scratchpad/evren-setup.ps1" <<'EOF'
# EVREN LLM API -> Continue kurulumu. Anahtar hicbir yere loglanmaz.
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$base = "https://evren-llmapi.ssyz.org.tr/v1"
$cfg  = "$HOME\.continue\config.yaml"

$sec = Read-Host "EVREN API anahtariniz (evren_llm_...)" -AsSecureString
$key = [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::PtrToStringAuto(
         [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::SecureStringToBSTR($sec))

if (-not $key.StartsWith("evren_llm_")) {
  Write-Host "Why: anahtar 'evren_llm_' ile baslamiyor." -ForegroundColor Red
  Write-Host "Fix: /api-keys sayfasindan anahtari tam kopyalayin (bosluk/yeni satir olmadan)."
  exit 2
}
$h = @{ "X-API-Key" = $key }

# 1) Anahtar gercekten gecerli mi?
try { $models = Invoke-RestMethod "$base/models" -Headers $h }
catch {
  Write-Host "Why: anahtar gecidde dogrulanmadi ($($_.Exception.Response.StatusCode.value__))." -ForegroundColor Red
  Write-Host "Fix: anahtari /api-keys sayfasinda silip yeniden olusturun."
  exit 1
}
Write-Host ("OK  /v1/models -> {0} model" -f $models.data.Count) -ForegroundColor Green

# 2) Sartlar (atlanirsa 403 terms_not_accepted)
$st = Invoke-RestMethod "$base/terms/status" -Headers $h
if (-not $st.accepted) {
  Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post "$base/terms/accept" -Headers $h `
    -ContentType "application/json" -Body (@{ version = $st.current_version } | ConvertTo-Json) | Out-Null
  Write-Host ("OK  sartlar onaylandi (v{0})" -f $st.current_version) -ForegroundColor Green
} else {
  Write-Host ("OK  sartlar zaten onayli (v{0})" -f $st.current_version) -ForegroundColor Green
}

# 3) Gercek bir cagri
$body = @{ model = "auto"; messages = @(@{ role = "user"; content = "Merhaba" }); max_tokens = 2048 } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
$r = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post "$base/chat/completions" -Headers $h -ContentType "application/json" -Body $body
Write-Host ("OK  sohbet -> {0}: {1}" -f $r.model, $r.choices[0].message.content) -ForegroundColor Green

# 4) Kota
$q = Invoke-RestMethod "$base/quota" -Headers $h
Write-Host ("OK  kalan kota: {0}" -f ($q | ConvertTo-Json -Compress)) -ForegroundColor Green

# 5) Config'i yamala (yedek alarak)
Copy-Item $cfg "$cfg.bak" -Force
(Get-Content $cfg -Raw).Replace("BURAYA_EVREN_ANAHTARINIZ", $key) | Set-Content $cfg -Encoding utf8 -NoNewline
Write-Host "OK  config.yaml yamalandi. VSCode'da Continue panelini kapatip acin." -ForegroundColor Green
EOF
echo "olusturuldu"

# EVREN LLM Gateway — Kullanım Şartları ve Kabul Edilebilir Kullanım Politikası

![Versiyon](https://img.shields.io/badge/versiyon-1-blue) ![Durum](https://img.shields.io/badge/durum-esaslı%20(v1%2C%20ilk%20yayın)-orange)

> Bu belge **v1**'dir — EVREN LLM Gateway'in ilk yayın sürümü. Bu sürüm **esaslı**
> (`is_material=true`) sayılır: gateway'i kullanan her hesap, ilk API çağrısından
> önce bu metni açıkça kabul etmelidir (`POST /v1/terms/accept`). Sonraki sürümler
> yalnızca **esaslı değişiklik** taşıyorsa yeniden kabul tetikler; salt kozmetik/
> yazım düzeltmeleri tetiklemez.

---

## 1. Kapsam

Bu şartlar, `api.evren.<domain>` üzerinden sunulan OpenAI-uyumlu LLM Gateway'in
(`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/models` ve
ilgili tüm uçlar) kullanımını kapsar. API anahtarı oluşturan veya LLM Chat
Portal'ı kullanan her hesap bu şartlara tabidir.

## 2. Kabul Edilebilir Kullanım

Aşağıdaki kullanımlar **yasaktır**:

- Yasadışı, zararlı veya üçüncü tarafların haklarını ihlal eden içerik üretimi.
- Kritik altyapıya yönelik saldırı hazırlığı veya kolaylaştırılması.
- Reşit olmayanlara zarar verecek içerik.
- Barındırılan modellerin kendi lisans şartlarında (bkz.
  `docs/compliance/LLM_MODEL_LICENSE_REVIEW.md`) tanımlı kullanım-bazlı
  kısıtlamaların ihlali.
- Hız sınırlarını, kota mekanizmalarını veya kimlik doğrulamasını atlatmaya
  yönelik teknik girişimler (rate-limit bypass, anahtar paylaşımı, otomatik
  hesap oluşturma).

EVREN, `content_guard` (prompt güvenlik sınıflandırması) ve `content_policy`
(Wave 1 metin-dışı içerik reddi) katmanlarıyla bu politikayı teknik olarak
kısmen uygular — ama nihai sorumluluk kullanıcıdadır.

## 3. Faturalama ve Kredi Ekonomisi

Kullanım, HOLD → SETTLE zinciriyle kredi (CR) cinsinden faturalanır. Kesin
tutarlar `/v1/models` ve admin fiyatlandırma panelinde şeffaf şekilde
yayınlanır. Beklenmeyen kesinti (gateway çökmesi, ağ kesintisi) durumunda
`billing_pending` mekanizması devreye girer — bkz. dahili mühendislik
belgeleri, kullanıcıya karşı garanti bu belgenin kapsamı dışıdır.

## 4. Veri İşleme ve KVKK

Kullanım verileri (prompt/completion metni) KVKK kapsamında işlenir — org
düzeyinde rıza (`llm_corpus_consent`) ve kullanıcı düzeyinde unutulma hakkı
(`llm_privacy_tombstone`) mekanizmaları mevcuttur. Detaylar
`docs/compliance/` altındaki ayrı KVKK belgelerinde ele alınır.

## 5. Hizmet Seviyesi ve Sorumluluk Sınırı

Hizmet "olduğu gibi" sağlanır. EVREN, barındırılan modellerin çıktılarının
doğruluğunu garanti etmez. Planlı/plansız kesintilerde en iyi çaba (best-effort)
telafi (kısmi/tam kredi iadesi) uygulanır — kesin SLA taahhüdü bu belgenin
kapsamı dışıdır, ayrı bir ticari sözleşmenin konusudur.

## 6. Fesih

EVREN, bu şartların ihlali durumunda hesabı/API anahtarını askıya alma veya
sonlandırma hakkını saklı tutar. Kullanıcı, API anahtarını istediği zaman
admin panelinden devre dışı bırakabilir.

## 7. Değişiklikler

- **Esaslı değişiklik** (`is_material=true`): fiyatlandırma modeli, veri
  işleme kapsamı, sorumluluk sınırları gibi kullanıcı kararını etkileyecek
  maddelerde değişiklik — yeni sürüm yayınlanır, TÜM kullanıcılar yeniden
  kabul etmeden gateway'i kullanamaz.
- **Kozmetik değişiklik** (`is_material=false`): yazım düzeltmesi, netleştirme
  — yeniden kabul TETİKLEMEZ, ama denetim kaydı için yeni bir versiyon satırı
  yine oluşturulur.

---

*Bu belge bir hukuk ekibi tarafından nihai olarak gözden geçirilmemiştir —
platformun ilk yayın öncesi taslak sürümüdür.*

Bitti. Şartlar onaylandı, geçit doğrulandı, Continue yapılandırıldı.

**Doğrulama sonuçları:**
- `POST /v1/terms/accept` → `accepted_version: 1`, `accepted_at: 2026-10-18T21:32:14Z`
- `POST /v1/chat/completions` (`model: auto`) → `google/gemma-4-31b` üzerinden yanıt geldi, 130 token
- `GET /v1/models` → 17 model erişilebilir (403 kalktı)
- Kota → günlük 15.000.000 token'ın 14.999.870'i duruyor, 00:00 UTC'de sıfırlanıyor
- Continue `config.yaml` → 6 placeholder gerçek anahtarla değişti, yedek `config.yaml.bak` olarak duruyor

**Şimdi yapmanız gereken:** Kilo Code'da aynı istemi tekrar gönderin — onay hesap düzeyinde olduğu için eklentide hiçbir ayara dokunmanız gerekmiyor. Continue için paneli bir kez kapatıp açın, model seçicide 4 sohbet modeli ("GLM 5.3", "MiMo v2.6 Pro", "DeepSeek v4.1 Flash", "Gemma 4 31B") belirir; `@codebase` için embedding ve reranker de bağlı.

**Anahtar hijyeni — buna dikkat edin:** Anahtar artık bu sohbet geçmişinde düz metin olarak duruyor. Depo temiz (`git grep` ile doğruladım, izlenen hiçbir dosyada yok) ve config kullanıcı profilinizde, repo dışında. Yine de şartların 2. maddesi anahtar paylaşımını açıkça yasak sayıyor; entegrasyonun çalıştığını gördükten sonra `/api-keys` sayfasından bu anahtarı iptal edip yenisini oluşturmanızı öneririm. Onay hesap düzeyinde olduğu için yeni anahtar hiçbir ek adım gerektirmeden çalışır — sadece Kilo'daki ve `config.yaml`'daki değeri güncellemeniz yeter, isterseniz onu da yaparım.

İsterseniz opencode ve Codex CLI yapılandırmalarını da aynı şekilde yazabilirim; ikisi de artık onaylı hesapla doğrudan çalışacak durumda.

EVREN tarafı bitti — 31.7 t/s ile yanıt geliyor. ripgrep hatası bambaşka bir sorundu ve kök nedeni buldum:

## ripgrep hatası: neden ve çözüm

**Neden:** VSCode 1.142, ripgrep'i `@vscode/ripgrep/bin/rg.exe` yolundan `@vscode/ripgrep-universal/bin/win32-x64/rg.exe` yoluna taşımış. Kilo'nun `bin/kilo.exe` dosyası hâlâ eski yolu arıyor (binary içinde `@vscode/ripgrep` string'i duruyor), bulamıyor ve yedek plan olarak GitHub'dan indirmeye düşüyor — orada da takılıyor. Yolu dışarıdan düzeltecek bir env değişkeni de yok; `kilo.exe` içindeki değişkenleri taradım, ripgrep yolu için override yok.

İlginç olan: GitHub bu makineden erişilebilir durumda (aynı URL'i `curl` ile çektim, HTTP 200, 1.25s). Yani indirme hatası ağ genelinde değil, eklentinin kendi ağ yolunda — proxy ya da antivirüs kaynaklı. Bu yüzden "tekrar dene" demek yerine indirmeye hiç ihtiyaç bırakmayan çözümü kurdum.

**Yapılan:** VSCode'un kendi ripgrep'ini (15.0.0) Kilo'nun beklediği yola kopyaladım:

```
...\Microsoft VS Code\6d62b1d5da\resources\app\node_modules\@vscode\ripgrep\bin\rg.exe
```

Doğruladım: binary çalışıyor (`ripgrep 15.0.0`) ve gerçek bir dosya aramasını `portable_agent_kit` üzerinde başarıyla döndürüyor.

**Şimdi:** VSCode'da `Developer: Reload Window` çalıştırın — Kilo rg yolunu oturum başında bir kez çözüyor, yeniden yüklenmeden eski başarısız sonucu kullanmaya devam eder.

**Bilmeniz gereken tek şey:** VSCode güncellendiğinde `6d62b1d5da` klasörü yeni sürüm hash'iyle değişeceği için bu kopya kaybolur ve hata geri döner. O zaman tek komut yeter (hash'i yeni klasöre göre günceller):

```powershell
$app = (Get-ChildItem "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Microsoft VS Code" -Directory |
        Where-Object { Test-Path "$($_.FullName)\resources\app" } | Select-Object -First 1).FullName + "\resources\app"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$app\node_modules\@vscode\ripgrep\bin" | Out-Null
Copy-Item "$app\node_modules.asar.unpacked\@vscode\ripgrep-universal\bin\win32-x64\rg.exe" `
          "$app\node_modules\@vscode\ripgrep\bin\rg.exe" -Force
```

Geri almak isterseniz: `node_modules\@vscode\ripgrep` klasörünü silmek yeterli, VSCode'un kendi dosyalarına dokunmadım.

## Voidfarer

Ajan projeyi bulamadı çünkü araması çalışmıyordu — proje aslında zaten açık olan çalışma alanının içinde: [projects/voidfarer](projects/voidfarer). İçinde `.aikit`, kendi `.git` deposu, 14 KB README, `tests/`, `voidfarer/` paketi ve `play.bat` var; oyunun kayıt dosyası da `C:\Users\Yunus-Emre\AppData\Local\.voidfarer\voidfarer_save.json` (dün 00:01'de güncellenmiş, yanında `.bak`). Reload sonrası aynı istemi tekrar verdiğinizde Kilo bunu sorunsuz bulacak.

Kalan tek şey o `Get-ChildItem` izin istemi — onu onaylamak sizin kararınız; salt-okunur bir listeleme olduğu için Kilo'nun auto-approve kurallarına eklenmesi makul, ama yazma/çalıştırma yetkilerini otomatik onaya almamanızı öneririm.

# AIKit Operational Runbook (Universal Host Integration)

This operational runbook provides the unified command matrix for driving AIKit across all supported agent host clients (Antigravity, Claude, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Cline) under **PRINCIPLE-009 R7** (Pluggable Host Architecture) and **PRINCIPLE-017 R2** (Cross-IDE Synchronization).

---

## 🌐 Host Client Operation Matrix

- **Antigravity**: Native chat harness. Discovers this skill via `.agents/skills/aikit/SKILL.md` and rule files in `.agents/rules/`.
- **Claude (Code CLI / Desktop)**: Reads `CLAUDE.md` automatically on startup. Discovers this skill natively via `.claude/skills/aikit/SKILL.md`. Executes kit commands directly via terminal tool calls.
- **OpenCode**: Runs headless subagent profiles (`architect`, `coder`, `tester`, etc.) via `opencode run --standalone` and slash commands via `opencode.jsonc`.
- **Cursor / VS Code / Windsurf / Cline**: Loads `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.windsurfrules`, `.clinerules`. Runs terminal commands.
- **State SSOT**: All clients interact with workspace state strictly through `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py` and `.agents/task_ledger.json` (a project's: `.aikit/task_ledger.json`).

---

## 🧱 Projects: Building Software Other Than AIKit (PRINCIPLE-011 R8)
The user's software lives in its own project, never in AIKit's tree:
```bash
python aikit.py list                 # which projects exist
python aikit.py new <name>           # projects/<name>/, seeds multi-IDE instruction guidelines
python aikit.py attach <path>        # an existing folder
python aikit.py status <name>        # its task, changes, latest decision and its gates
python aikit.py check <name>         # its Phase 4: tests, stack gates, hygiene, guidelines, secret scan; exit 0 to commit
python aikit.py guideline <name> "<rule>" --source user   # a project rule, below the principles
python aikit.py publish <name> [--public]   # its own GitHub repo; only when the user asks
python aikit.py fix <name>           # self-heals memory, cleans stale temp buffers, syncs codebase map
python aikit.py checkpoint <name>    # disruption checkpoint on the project ledger
python aikit.py resume <name>        # disruption resume on the project
python aikit.py complete <name>      # mark project task complete
python aikit.py clean <name>         # clean dangling project buffers
```
- Request names no single project: ask which one, or the name of a new one, before writing code.
- Before writing code in a project, read its guidelines (`status` or `resume` prints them): its own rules, which add to the principles and never override one (PRINCIPLE-000 R6). When the user states a lasting rule for the project, record it with `aikit guideline`.
- In the steps below, project work replaces the repository with the project: use the cockpit subcommands above, or add `--workspace <project path>` to every `disruption_recovery.py` command, write ADRs in `<project>/.aikit/decisions.md`, stage and commit inside the project, and run `python aikit.py check <name>` as Phase 4. `aikit fix <name>` self-heals project memory and cleans temporary buffers. AIKit's other gates are for changes to AIKit only.
- The project check runs the built-in hygiene scan of its source and static assets: mark a deliberate finding's own line `hygiene: allow <reason>`. After the check passes, record the checklist outcome (`checklists: passed`, or the failed or skipped item IDs) in the task's latest checkpoint description before the commit (PRINCIPLE-001 R8, PRINCIPLE-011 R8).

---

## 🤝 Delegating to Sub-Agents (PRINCIPLE-008 R6, PRINCIPLE-012 R8)
- **Claude Code**: hand bounded work to the project sub-agents in `.claude/agents/` through the Agent tool: `explorer` (searches, haiku), `worker` (docs and boilerplate, haiku), `architect` (read-only design), `reviewer` (audits, runs read-only gates), `tester` and `coder` (sonnet). Brief each with the milestone, the files it may change and the commands that verify it; run Phase 4 on what comes back.
- **Other hosts**: `python aikit.py delegate <role> "<brief>" [--project <name>]` runs the same role through OpenCode, on free models only: `architect` and `reviewer` on Gemini 3.8 Flash (needs `GEMINI_API_KEY` in the environment), the rest on OpenCode `-free` models (no key). A paid `--model` is refused (ADR-132).
- Roles have one text, `.opencode/agents/<role>.md`; `python scripts/sync_principles.py` regenerates the Claude copies. No agent can Edit or Write a task ledger (`.claude/settings.json`).

## 🧭 Phase 1: Orientation & Cold-Start Recovery

### 1. Resume Interrupted Tasks
Run on session startup, cold starts, or after a context compaction:
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --resume
```
- If an interrupted task is found, resume from its recommended phase.
- If uncommitted files or orphaned buffers exist, inspect them before proceeding.

### 2. Disruption Recovery Audit
Inspect the entire repository status, active task, and dangling temporary files:
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --audit
```

### 3. Change Track Classification
Determine whether proposed edits require formal checklists:
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --track
```
- **Track A**: Zero edits / read-only investigation.
- **Track B**: Documentation, comments, and non-rule markdown. Requires Post-Flight checklist and secret scan.
- **Track C**: Code, rules, workflows, or schemas. Full lifecycle verification required.

---

## 📋 Phase 2: Checkpointing & Planning (Track C Gate)

### 1. Pre-Flight Checklist
Review before making any code modifications on Track C tasks:
- Freshness: Read target files in slices before writing (PRINCIPLE-003 R1).
- Call Sites: Grep all symbol references across the repository before refactoring (PRINCIPLE-003 R2).
- Zero Undeclared Deps: Only use standard-library modules or explicitly declared dependencies (PRINCIPLE-003 R3).
- Platform Parity: Use `pathlib.Path` and avoid shell-specific builtins (PRINCIPLE-003 R4).

### 2. Record Micro-Milestones
Checkpoint plan with explicit impact assessment (`--why`, `--benefits`, `--risks`, `--mitigation`):
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --checkpoint <task_id> --phase-num 2 --desc "[1/M] Planning and architectural design" --why "<motivation>" --benefits "<gains>" --risks "contract: ...; dependency: ...; concurrency: ...; state: ..." --mitigation "<strategy>"
```
- Bound milestone count to $M \le 6$ (PRINCIPLE-008 R3).

---

## 🛠️ Phase 3: Implementation & Synchronization

### 1. Synchronize Principles & IDE Instructions
After modifying `GUIDELINES.md` or `.agents/rules/domain.md`, update all 8 host client instruction files and README:
```bash
python scripts/sync_principles.py
```
- Verify zero budget violations (<1,600 tokens per target):
```bash
python scripts/sync_principles.py --check
```

### 2. Synchronize AST Codebase Map & Knowledge Base
After creating or refactoring symbols:
```bash
python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py
```
- Verify link integrity and codebase map freshness:
```bash
python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py --check
```

### 3. Subagent Delegation via OpenCode (PRINCIPLE-012 R8)
Delegate bulk token-heavy work to free or local subagents using headless non-interactive mode:
```bash
# High-speed grep and symbol exploration
opencode run --standalone --format json --agent explorer "<query>"

# Architecture & deep reasoning (SWE-bench 49.2%)
opencode run --standalone --format json --agent architect "<prompt>"

# High-fidelity code refactoring (SWE-bench 39.8%)
opencode run --standalone --format json --agent coder --file <target> "<prompt>"

# Automated test creation and regression verification
opencode run --standalone --format json --agent tester --file <test_file> "<prompt>"

# Documentation, link and claim-fidelity audit
opencode run --standalone --format json --agent reviewer "<audit_prompt>"

# Offline / Air-gapped code generation via local Ollama
opencode run --standalone --format json --agent coder --model ollama/qwen2.5-coder:latest --auto "<prompt>"
```
*(Subagents MUST NOT write to the ledger; only the root orchestrator writes checkpoints).*

---

## 🔒 Phase 4: Verification Gate Shield (Pre-Commit Delivery Triad)

Before committing any Track B or Track C changes, ALL gates must pass:

### 1. Test Suite Verification (100% Pass Required)
```bash
# Sub-second unit test suite (<1s budget)
python -m unittest tests.test_kit

# Integration test suite (<5s budget)
python -m unittest tests.test_integration
```

### 2. Read-Only Quality Gates
```bash
# Rule and budget freshness check
python scripts/sync_principles.py --check

# AST and knowledge base check
python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py --check

# Secret and credential scan
python scripts/check_secrets.py --all

# Invariant reachability shield
python scripts/check_reachability.py

# Universal operational dogfooding runner
python scripts/dogfood.py
```

---

## 🚀 Phase 5: Delivery & Git Operations

### 1. Mark Task Completed
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --complete <task_id>
```

### 2. Purge Dangling Temp Files
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --clean
```

### 3. Conventional Commit Validation
```bash
python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --validate-commit "<type>(<scope>): <subject>"
```

### 4. Explicit Staging & Non-Destructive Recoil
```bash
# Stage modified files explicitly by name (NEVER git add .)
git add <file1> <file2> ...

# Commit
git commit -m "<type>(<scope>): <subject>"
```

content.content:
- **Concept**: Governance is split into two tiers. Tier 1 is a generated set of one-line capsules that every agent loads automatically. Tier 2 is the full rule text in `GUIDELINES.md`, read one section at a time when a named trigger fires. Every rule names who it binds and what to do; rules about files are checked by `scripts/sync_principles.py` and the test suite, and rules about agent conduct are checked by the report that R8 requires.
--
- **Invariant**: Pre-Flight checklist before the first Track C edit; Post-Flight checklist before any Track B or C commit; report only failed items (R8).

    raise AssertionError(

    def test_every_external_program_the_scripts_run_is_declared(self):
        # Red-green pin: R3 requires declared dependencies, yet the scripts ran `git` while the
        # README prerequisites said "Standard Library only".
        os_bundled = {"taskkill"}  # ships with Windows; governed by R4, not R3
        prerequisites = next(l for l in README_MD.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
                             if "Runtime Prerequisites" in l)
        for script in sorted((ROOT_DIR / "scripts").glob("*.py")):
            source = script.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            # What actually executes: the first element of a list handed straight to
            # subprocess.run/Popen, or a wrapper's ["<program>", *args]. Wrapper arguments such as
            # git_output(["diff", ...]) are subcommands, not programs.
            executed = set(re.findall(r'subprocess\.(?:run|Popen)\(\s*\[\s*"([a-z][\w.-]*)"', source))
            executed |= set(re.findall(r'\[\s*"([a-z][\w.-]*)",\s*\*args\]', source))
            for program in executed:
                if program in os_bundled or program.startswith("-"):
                    continue
                with self.subTest(script=script.name, program=program):

        # scripts continue on silent guesses - e.g. an unreadable backup silently became an empty
        # ledger, and a failed audit scan reported "clean".
        import ast
        for script in sorted((ROOT_DIR / "scripts").glob("*.py")):
            # The shared content-keyed cache: the knowledge-base tests parse these same files.
            tree = parse_source(script.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), str(script))
            for node in ast.walk(tree):
                if not isinstance(node, ast.ExceptHandler) or node.type is None:
                    continue
                broad = "Exception" in ast.dump(node.type) and "Error" not in ast.dump(node.type)
                silent = all(isinstance(b, (ast.Pass, ast.Return, ast.Continue)) for b in node.body)
                with self.subTest(script=script.name, line=node.lineno):
                    self.assertFalse(broad and silent,
                                     f"{script.name}:{node.lineno} swallows Exception silently")

    def test_user_facing_commands_use_python_not_py(self):
        # R4 + PRINCIPLE-011 R6: a remediation command must work when copy-pasted on any OS; the
        # `py` launcher exists only on Windows.
        for path in [*sorted((ROOT_DIR / "scripts").glob("*.py")), SSOT_MD, README_MD]:
            with self.subTest(file=path.name):
                self.assertNotRegex(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), r"(?<![\w-])py scripts/")

    def test_unmeasurable_disk_space_is_announced(self):
        real = shutil.disk_usage

content.text:
Durdum — buradan ötesi sizin kararınız, çünkü her yol ya testi zayıflatıyor (PRINCIPLE-014: kullanıcı onayı + ADR şart) ya da bir principle bütçesini değiştiriyor (PRINCIPLE-000 R3: cross-principle check). Hiçbir dosyayı düzenlemedim; ağaç hâlâ `b4f9582`, yalnızca ledger bookkeeping'i değişti.

## Ölçümler

| Katman | Şimdi | Bütçe | Test başına |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | 1.21–1.45s / 317 test | <1s | 3.8ms |
| Integration | 7.76–8.21s / 45 test | <5s | 172ms |

**Unit'in maliyeti israf değil:** profilde 1047 gerçek dosya `open` çağrısı 0.37s tutuyor — suite'in %27'si. Bunun yalnızca ~55ms'i depo kaynaklarının tekrar tekrar okunması (ölçtüm: `scripts/*.py` 7 tam tarama 12ms, `GUIDELINES.md` 83 okuma 43ms). Geri kalanı ledger'ın atomik yazma, `.bak` ve advisory-lock testlerinin gerçek dosya işlemleri — PRINCIPLE-013 bunların gerçek olmasını şart koşuyor. AST ayrıştırma ve `fsync` zaten cache'li/stub'lı; toplanacak düşük meyve kalmamış. Yani ilk planımın [1/5] kaldıracı 250–450ms'lik açığın ~55ms'ini kapatıyor: yetersiz.

**Integration'ın tabanı sabit:** 35 gerçek CLI spawn × 100ms = 3.49s, üstüne tempdir'de gerçek `git init/add/commit` işi. En yavaş test (1.047s) zaten `python -c "pass"` gibi önemsiz bir nested test komutu kullanıyor — orada da israf yok. 2.8s kesmek, CLI sözleşme spawn'larının yaklaşık üçte birini veya git destekli testleri silmek demek.

## Üç yol

**A — Testleri taşı/azalt.** Ledger I/O ağırlıklı ~15 unit testini integration'a taşı (unit ~0.3s düşer, bütçeye girer), integration'daki 35 spawn'dan ~12'sini birleştir veya sil. Gerçek kapsama kaybı; PRINCIPLE-014 gereği sizin onayınız + ADR gerekiyor. Not: integration'a test taşımak o katmanı daha da bütçe dışına iter, yani ikisi birlikte çözülmezse çelişir.

**B — Bütçeleri test başına ifade et (önerim).** PRINCIPLE-010/014'teki mutlak duvar saati yerine test başına tavan: unit ≤5ms/test, integration ≤200ms/test. Bugün ikisi de geçiyor (3.8ms ve 172ms). Gerekçe: mutlak tavan suite büyüdükçe kaçınılmaz olarak ihlal edilir — kural yazıldığında suite bu kadar değildi; asıl niyet olan "hızlı geri bildirim, unit'te spawn/sleep yok" korunur ve ölçülebilir kalır. Bu bir gevşetmedir, bunu açıkça söylüyorum; ADR + 20 principle için cross-principle check ister.

**C — Aşımı bilinen sapma olarak kaydet.** Kural ve testler olduğu gibi kalır, ADR sapmayı ve nedenini belgeler. En az iş, ama her Post-Flight'ta PRINCIPLE-010 maddesi başarısız raporlanmaya devam eder.

Hangisini seçerseniz yeni bir `[1/M]` planı kontrol noktası açıp uygularım. B'yi seçerseniz kural metnini ben yazar, `sync_principles` ile 8 hedefi yeniler, ADR'yi cross-principle check'iyle ekler ve Phase 4'ü koştururum.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Invariant Reachability Shield (PRINCIPLE-014 Rule 7)

A passing test proves a mechanism works. It never proves the mechanism is *used*. The
highest-frequency defect class found in this repository was precisely that gap:

  - `file_lock()` was defined, exported and unit-tested with zero production call sites, so
    parallel agents silently erased each other's ledger checkpoints.
  - `format_resume_report()` read a `last_phase_num` key that no writer ever produced, so every
    resumption silently reported a default phase.

Both were green in CI. This checker closes the class mechanically by auditing two things across
production modules:

  1. Call-site reachability - every function must be called from production code or dispatched
     from an entrypoint. "A test calls it" is not reachability.
  2. Key round-trip integrity - every persisted-state key read must have a writer, and every
     key written should have a reader.

Zero external dependencies (standard library only).

Usage:
  python scripts/check_reachability.py [--verbose]
Exit codes:
  0 clean    1 unreachable capability or phantom key found    2 CLI argument misuse
"""

import ast
import sys

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Test Tier Budget Gate (PRINCIPLE-010 Rule 6, PRINCIPLE-014 Rule 3)

The two test tiers carry speed budgets because a slow tier stops being run. For months those
budgets were absolute wall-clock numbers that nothing measured:

  - the unit tier was budgeted under 1s and ran 1.21-1.45s for 317 tests;
  - the integration tier was budgeted under 5s and ran 7.63-7.94s for 45 tests.

Both drifted in unnoticed, because every Phase 4 command reported the tiers as green without
reporting how long they took. An absolute per-suite cap also cannot survive a growing suite:
adding a correct, fast test eventually breaks it, which pressures the agent to delete coverage.

This gate replaces the assumption with a measurement. It runs each tier exactly once, reads the
count and duration unittest itself prints, and compares the per-test average against the tier's
ceiling. It is the single way Phase 4 runs the tiers, so it adds no second run of its own.

Zero external dependencies (standard library only).

Usage:
  python scripts/check_test_budgets.py [--verbose]
Exit codes:
  0 every tier passed and stayed inside budget   1 a tier failed, exceeded budget or was unreadable   2 CLI argument misuse
"""

import re
import subprocess
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

ROOT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

# The ceiling each tier's average test may reach, in milliseconds. Measured over three runs
# including a cold filesystem cache: unit 3.59-5.84ms, integration 169.58-176.49ms (ADR-144).
TIER_BUDGETS_MS: Dict[str, float] = {
    "tests.test_kit": 8.0,
    "tests.test_integration": 200.0,
}

# A tier that hangs must fail the gate rather than block delivery for ever.
TIER_TIMEOUT = 300

_SUMMARY = re.compile(r"^Ran (\d+) tests? in ([0-9.]+)s", re.M)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TierResult:
    """One tier's measured outcome; frozen so a report cannot edit what was measured."""

    module: str
    tests: int
    seconds: float
    passed: bool

    @property
    def per_test_ms(self) -> float:
        return (self.seconds / self.tests * 1000.0) if self.tests else 0.0

    @property
    def budget_ms(self) -> float:
        return TIER_BUDGETS_MS[self.module]

    @property
    def inside_budget(self) -> bool:
        return self.per_test_ms <= self.budget_ms


def parse_tier_output(output: str) -> Optional[Tuple[int, float]]:
    """The count and duration unittest prints, or None when it never got that far."""
    match = _SUMMARY.search(output)
    if not match:
        return None
    return int(match.group(1)), float(match.group(2))


def default_runner(module: str, timeout: int) -> Tuple[int, str]:
    """Run one tier the way the runbook documents it, so the gate measures the real command."""
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "unittest", module],
        cwd=str(ROOT_DIR), capture_output=True, text=True,
        encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", timeout=timeout,
    )
    return proc.returncode, (proc.stdout or "") + (proc.stderr or "")


def run_tier(module: str, runner: Optional[Callable[[str, int], Tuple[int, str]]] = None) -> Optional[TierResult]:
    """Measure one tier, or None when its output carried no summary to measure."""
    code, output = (runner or default_runner)(module, TIER_TIMEOUT)
    summary = parse_tier_output(output)
    if summary is None:
        return None
    tests, seconds = summary
    return TierResult(module=module, tests=tests, seconds=seconds, passed=(code == 0))


def budget_errors(results: List[TierResult]) -> List[str]:
    """One line per tier that is over its ceiling; empty when every tier fits."""
    return [
        f"{r.module}: {r.per_test_ms:.2f}ms per test exceeds the {r.budget_ms:.2f}ms ceiling "
        f"({r.tests} tests in {r.seconds:.3f}s)"
        for r in results
        if not r.inside_budget
    ]


def run_check(runner: Optional[Callable[[str, int], Tuple[int, str]]] = None, verbose: bool = False) -> int:
    print("=" * 58)
    print("TEST TIER BUDGET GATE (PRINCIPLE-010 R6)")
    print("=" * 58)

    results: List[TierResult] = []
    failures: List[str] = []
    for module in TIER_BUDGETS_MS:
        result = run_tier(module, runner=runner)
        if result is None:
            failures.append(f"{module}: produced no test summary, so it could not be measured")
            print(f"[FAIL] {module}: no 'Ran N tests in Xs' summary; the tier did not run")
            continue
        results.append(result)
        if not result.passed:
            failures.append(f"{module}: the tier failed")
        verdict = "FAIL" if not result.passed else ("OVER" if not result.inside_budget else "PASS")
        print(f"[{verdict}] {module}: {result.tests} tests in {result.seconds:.3f}s "
              f"= {result.per_test_ms:.2f}ms per test (ceiling {result.budget_ms:.2f}ms)")

    over = budget_errors(results)
    for line in over:
        print(f"Why: {line}")
    if over:
        print("Fix: profile the tier and return the slowest tests to budget, or raise the ceiling "
              "in PRINCIPLE-010 R6 with an ADR and the user's approval (PRINCIPLE-014 R3).")
    if failures:
        for line in failures:
            print(f"Why: {line}")
        print("Fix: run the tier directly to see which test failed, then repair it before delivery.")

    if verbose:
        for r in results:
            print(f"   {r.module}: budget {r.budget_ms:.2f}ms, headroom "
                  f"{r.budget_ms - r.per_test_ms:.2f}ms per test")

    if not failures and not over:
        print(f"[OK] {len(results)} tier(s) passed and stayed inside budget.")
    print("=" * 58)
    return 1 if (failures or over) else 0


KNOWN_FLAGS = {"--verbose", "-v", "--help", "-h"}

HELP_TEXT = """AIKit Test Tier Budget Gate (PRINCIPLE-010 Rule 6)

Usage:
  python scripts/check_test_budgets.py [OPTIONS]

Runs every test tier once and fails when a tier fails, when its output carries no summary, or
when its average test exceeds the tier's ceiling. This is Phase 4's way of running the tiers, so
it replaces running them by hand rather than adding a second run.

Options:
  --verbose, -v   Print each tier's ceiling and remaining headroom
  -h, --help      Show this help message and exit

Exit codes:
  0  inside budget    1  tier failed, over budget or unreadable    2  CLI argument misuse
"""


if __name__ == "__main__":
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    if "-h" in argv or "--help" in argv:
        print(HELP_TEXT, end="")
        sys.exit(0)

    unknown = [a for a in argv if a.startswith("-") and a not in KNOWN_FLAGS]
    if unknown:
        print(f"[INVALID USAGE] Unrecognized option(s): {', '.join(unknown)}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(f"Why: this gate accepts only {', '.join(sorted(KNOWN_FLAGS))}.", file=sys.stderr)
        print("Fix: run 'python scripts/check_test_budgets.py --help' to list valid options.",
              file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)

    sys.exit(run_check(verbose=("--verbose" in argv or "-v" in argv)))

lines: ### PRINCIPLE-010: Performance & Resource Optimization (Speed & Lean Architecture)

- **Problem**: Quadratic loops, blocking I/O on event loops, hung subprocesses, disk thrashing from per-record `fsync`, daemon memory creep, heavy startup imports and slow test suites degrade performance and developer velocity. When a limit is stated twice with different numbers, or as "heavy" or "unbounded", each model applies a different one.
- **Concept**: Each performance limit is one number, stated once and measured by a test or a gate; the decidable resource rules are checked in every module.
-- **Invariant**: Stream uncontrolled input; threads only for steps >=200ms; timeout= on subprocess, with on open(); one fsync per file; `--help` <200ms; unit <1s, integ <5s.

+- **Invariant**: Stream uncontrolled input; threads only for steps >=200ms; timeout= on subprocess, with on open(); one fsync per file; `--help` <200ms; unit <=8ms/test, integ <=200ms/test (`scripts/check_test_budgets.py`).

1. **Algorithmic Stream Processing ($O(1)$ Auxiliary Memory)** *[Agent]*: A membership test inside a loop MUST use a `set` or `dict`, never a `list` or `tuple` that grows with the input. Input whose size the program does not control (user data, logs, network or process streams) MUST be read incrementally (iteration, `yield`, bounded chunks), never whole. Files the tool itself writes and bounds, such as its sources, rule files and the 20-entry ledger, MAY be read whole.

2. **Non-Blocking Event Loops & Measurement-Driven Concurrency** *[Agent]*: Inside `async` code or a GUI main thread, file, process, database and network calls MUST run through `asyncio.to_thread()` or a worker thread. Threads or processes MAY be added to a step only when that step, measured single-threaded, takes 200ms or more; the measurement is stated in the commit message or ADR.

3. **Subprocess Timeout Gate & Bounded Concurrency** *[Agent + Maintainer]*: Every `subprocess.run`, `call`, `check_call` and `check_output` passes `timeout=`, and every `Popen` is waited on with a timeout. Parallel processes are started through a pool of at most `os.cpu_count()` workers.

4. **Deterministic Resource Reclamation & Daemon Ring Buffers (RAII)** *[Agent + Maintainer]*: `open()` and `Path.open()` run only as a `with` item; a raw descriptor from `os.open` is closed in `try`/`finally`; other OS resources (sockets, handles, processes) are released in a `with` or `try`/`finally`. A process that runs until stopped keeps every growing collection bounded (`collections.deque(maxlen=N)`, a capped cache). `python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py` fails on a blocking subprocess call without `timeout=` and on `open()` outside a `with`.

5. **Batch I/O Coalescing & Cold Startup Budget** *[Agent + Maintainer]*: Code that writes many records to one file writes them all and then calls `os.fsync` once; one fsync per file written is PRINCIPLE-013 R1, not a violation.
