lines: ### PRINCIPLE-010: Performance & Resource Optimization (Speed & Lean Architecture)

- **Problem**: Quadratic loops, blocking I/O on event loops, hung subprocesses, disk thrashing from per-record `fsync`, daemon memory creep, heavy startup imports and slow test suites degrade performance and developer velocity. When a limit is stated twice with different numbers, or as "heavy" or "unbounded", each model applies a different one.
- **Concept**: Each performance limit is one number, stated once and measured by a test or a gate; the decidable resource rules are checked in every module.

-- **Invariant**: Stream uncontrolled input; threads only for steps >=200ms; timeout= on subprocess, with on open(); one fsync per file; `--help` <200ms; unit <=8ms, integ <=200ms per test (`check_test_budgets.py`).
+- **Invariant**: Stream uncontrolled input; threads only for steps >=200ms; timeout= on subprocess, with on open(); one fsync per file; `--help` <200ms; unit <=8ms, integ <=200ms per test.

1. **Algorithmic Stream Processing ($O(1)$ Auxiliary Memory)** *[Agent]*: A membership test inside a loop MUST use a `set` or `dict`, never a `list` or `tuple` that grows with the input. Input whose size the program does not control (user data, logs, network or process streams) MUST be read incrementally (iteration, `yield`, bounded chunks), never whole. Files the tool itself writes and bounds, such as its sources, rule files and the 20-entry ledger, MAY be read whole.

2. **Non-Blocking Event Loops & Measurement-Driven Concurrency** *[Agent]*: Inside `async` code or a GUI main thread, file, process, database and network calls MUST run through `asyncio.to_thread()` or a worker thread. Threads or processes MAY be added to a step only when that step, measured single-threaded, takes 200ms or more; the measurement is stated in the commit message or ADR.
### PRINCIPLE-014: Automated Test Verification & Continuous Test Coverage (Regression Shield)

- **Problem**: Changes without tests break contracts; agents weaken or delete failing assertions to pass gates; shared state makes tests order-dependent; tests that only echo mocks prove nothing; leaked files pollute the tree. When "weaken" is undefined and two principles name different exceptions for changing a test, each model decides alone when a test may change.

- **Concept**: Every behaviour change arrives with a test that fails without it; a test changes only to become stricter, or with the user's approval recorded in an ADR; tests run fast, isolated and deterministic; and every safety mechanism is shown to be used, not only to work.

-- **Invariant**: 100% test pass gate; behaviour change = failing-first test; weakening a test needs user approval + ADR naming it; unit <=8ms/test, no spawns/sleeps; integration <=200ms/test; tempdir + addCleanup; reachability shield (`scripts/check_reachability.py`).

+- **Invariant**: 100% test pass gate; behaviour change = failing-first test; weakening a test needs user approval + ADR naming it; unit <=8ms/test, no spawns/sleeps; integration <=200ms/test; tempdir + addCleanup; `scripts/check_reachability.py`.

1. **Test-Backed Changes & Regression Shield** *[Agent]*: A change that alters observable behaviour (a return value, output, written file, exit code or raised exception) MUST add or change a test in `tests/` that fails on the code before the change and passes after it. A change that keeps behaviour, such as a refactor or a comment, needs no new test; every existing test MUST pass unchanged.

2. **Test Sanctity Invariant (Anti-Regression Masking)** *[Agent]*: *Weakening* a test is any change after which it accepts a behaviour it rejected before: deleting or skipping it, removing or loosening an assertion, widening an allowlist or threshold. Rewording a test so that it rejects the same behaviours, or more, is not weakening. When a test fails, the agent fixes the code. It MAY weaken a test only when the user approved the contract change the test encodes, and the ADR of that change names the test and the approval (PRINCIPLE-000 R5).

1. **Automatic Conventional Commits** *[Agent]*: When Phase 4 passes for a milestone or a task (PRINCIPLE-006 R1), the agent commits, unless the user said not to commit; then it stops after Phase 4 and reports the uncommitted files. The subject is `type(scope): description` or `type(scope): [milestone N/M] description`, with a type from `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `chore`, `test`, `perf`, `build`, `ci`, and at most 72 characters; `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --validate-commit "<message>"` MUST pass before the commit.

2. **Explicit Staging Invariant (Zero Blind Staging)** *[Agent]*: The agent stages files only by name (`git add <file> ...`). It MUST NOT run `git add .`, `git add -A`, `git add --all`, `git add -u` or `git commit -a`.

-  3. **Pre-Commit Delivery Triad Gate** *[Agent]*: No hook enforces this; except when the informed override of PRINCIPLE-002 R5 applies, the agent MUST NOT commit until all three hold on the tree being committed: (1) both test tiers pass; (2) every read-only gate passes: `python scripts/sync_principles.py --check`, `python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py --check`, `python scripts/check_reachability.py`, `python scripts/check_secrets.py` and `python scripts/dogfood.py`; (3) `git status --short` shows exactly the files the change intends staged, and nothing else modified. Items (1) and (2) are Phase 4 (PRINCIPLE-002 R1).

+  3. **Pre-Commit Delivery Triad Gate** *[Agent]*: No hook enforces this; except when the informed override of PRINCIPLE-002 R5 applies, the agent MUST NOT commit until all three hold on the tree being committed: (1) both test tiers pass, which `python scripts/check_test_budgets.py` verifies together with their per-test budgets (PRINCIPLE-010 R6); (2) every read-only gate passes: `python scripts/sync_principles.py --check`, `python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py --check`, `python scripts/check_reachability.py`, `python scripts/check_secrets.py` and `python scripts/dogfood.py`; (3) `git status --short` shows exactly the files the change intends staged, and nothing else modified. Items (1) and (2) are Phase 4 (PRINCIPLE-002 R1).

4. **Adaptive Push & Zero Force Push** *[Agent]*: After a commit the agent pushes to the current branch's upstream, unless the user said not to push. A branch without an upstream is pushed with `git push -u origin <branch>` when a remote named `origin` exists; with no remote it reports the commit as local only, and with remotes but none named `origin` it asks the user which to use. When the push is rejected because the remote moved, it runs `git pull --rebase` and pushes again; when the rebase stops on a conflict, it runs `git rebase --abort` and asks the user (PRINCIPLE-003 R6). It MUST NOT run `git push --force` or `--force-with-lease` unless the user asked for that push.

5. **Non-Destructive Recoil Invariant** *[Agent]*: To undo its own commit that is not yet pushed, the agent runs `git reset --soft HEAD^` (the parent commit); to undo a pushed commit, `git revert <hash>`. It MUST NOT run `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, `git checkout -- <file>`, `git restore <file>` or `git stash drop` on changes it did not make in this task.

6. **Terse Delivery Confirmation** *[Agent]*: The final message names, for every commit made, its short hash (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`), its subject, the number of files and the branch, and says whether it was pushed.

- **Date**: 2026-10-19
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: PRINCIPLE-010 R6 and PRINCIPLE-014 R3 budgeted the tiers as absolute wall clock, under 1s and under 5s. Both had been over budget for some time and no Phase 4 command measured either, so the breach drifted in unreported. Profiling showed the cost is not waste: 1047 real file opens cost 0.37s of the unit tier, most of them the atomic-write, backup and advisory-lock paths PRINCIPLE-013 requires to be real, and the integration tier has a 3.49s floor from 35 real CLI spawns at 100ms each. Caching the repeated reads of tracked sources saves only 55ms. An absolute per-suite cap also punishes growth: adding a correct, fast test eventually breaches it, which pressures the agent to delete coverage, exactly what PRINCIPLE-014 R2 forbids.
- **Decision**: Express both budgets as a per-test average and measure them. PRINCIPLE-010 R6 becomes a per-test ceiling of 8ms for the unit tier and 200ms for the integration tier, enforced by the new `scripts/check_test_budgets.py`, which runs each tier once, reads the count and duration unittest prints, and fails when a tier fails, when its output carries no summary, or when its average exceeds the ceiling. PRINCIPLE-018 R3 item (1) names that gate, so Phase 4 runs the tiers through it instead of twice. The ceilings leave 37% and 13% headroom over the slowest measured run. The user approved this relaxation explicitly; under PRINCIPLE-014 R2's exception this ADR names the two tests whose pinned wording changed with it, `test_principle_014_regression_shield_capsule` and `test_capsules_retain_their_mechanisms_after_condensation`, both of which still require the capsule to state the tier budgets and lost no strength.
- **Consequences**: A budget breach is now reported by a gate instead of being noticed by accident, and the gate prints each tier's average on every run. Raising a ceiling needs the user's approval and an ADR, so the measurement cannot be quietly widened. The capsule additions were paid for under PRINCIPLE-001 R9 by dropping the narrative label "reachability shield" from PRINCIPLE-014's capsule, which keeps the script path itself, and by abbreviating "integration" to "integ"; the tool name lives in PRINCIPLE-010 R6 and PRINCIPLE-018 R3, which are Tier 2 and unbudgeted. One stale reference stays by design: `knowledge/principles_audit_ledger.md` declares itself a snapshot that is not kept current (ADR-117), and its note on threshold flapping on loaded CI runners is the defect this ADR fixes.
- Cross-principle check: {cross}. PRINCIPLE-010 R6 and PRINCIPLE-014 R3 now state the same per-test numbers and cite each other, so the conflict between them cannot reopen; PRINCIPLE-018 R3 gained the gate command and keeps its triad unchanged; PRINCIPLE-013's real atomic-write paths are the reason the unit tier cannot be made arbitrarily fast and are left untouched; PRINCIPLE-001 R9's condensation rule was followed by cutting narrative, never a mechanism.
"""
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.rstrip("\n") + "\n" + adr)
print("ADR-144 eklendi")

Profiling showed the cost is not waste: 1047 real file opens cost 0.37s of the unit tier, most of them the atomic-write, backup and advisory-lock paths PRINCIPLE-013 requires to be real, and the integration tier has a 3.49s floor from 35 real CLI spawns at 100ms each. An absolute per-suite cap also punishes growth: adding a correct, fast test eventually breaches it, which pressures the agent to delete coverage, exactly what PRINCIPLE-014 R2 forbids.

PRINCIPLE-010 R6 becomes a per-test ceiling of 8ms for the unit tier and 200ms for the integration tier, enforced by the new `scripts/check_test_budgets.py`, which runs each tier once, reads the count and duration unittest prints, and fails when a tier fails, when its output carries no summary, or when its average exceeds the ceiling. | **Record Task Checkpoint**   | `python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --checkpoint <task_id> --phase-num <1-5> --desc <text>` | Appends a checkpoint (PRINCIPLE-002 R4); exits 2 when a task's first plan lacks `--why --benefits --risks --mitigation`, and warns when a task reaches Phase 3 with none (PRINCIPLE-007 R1, R6) |

## 🚀 Start a Project

Open this folder in any AI host and describe what to build. Each project gets its own folder under `projects/` (ignored by AIKit's git) and its own git repository; AIKit's gates, map and ledger never read it.

```bash
python aikit.py new my-app          # projects/my-app/: new git repo + .aikit/ memory
python aikit.py attach ../existing  # register a folder elsewhere; adds only .aikit/ and .gitignore lines
python aikit.py list                # every project, its stack and test command
python aikit.py status my-app       # its task, open changes, last decision
python aikit.py check my-app        # its tests, configured checks, hygiene, guidelines, secrets
python aikit.py check my-app --strict  # delivery: clean tree + map
python aikit.py fix my-app          # restore memory/README, refresh map, then check
python aikit.py guideline my-app "money is integer cents" --source user  # project rule
python aikit.py publish my-app      # own private GitHub repo, scanned first
```
A project's memory is its `.aikit/` folder (record, ledger, decisions, guidelines: its own rules, below the principles), committed in its repository; ledger commands take `--workspace projects/<name>`. Stack and test command are detected from its files (Python, Node, Rust, Go, Java, .NET); `--test "<cmd>"` overrides. `check` asks you to record `checklists: passed` or the failed IDs in the task's latest checkpoint before the commit (PRINCIPLE-001 R8, PRINCIPLE-011 R8); a deliberate hygiene finding needs `hygiene: allow <reason>` on its own line.

## 📥 Alternative: Copy AIKit Into an Existing Project

### Step 1: Copy Governance Assets

- Copy the source of truth and tooling; Tier 1 files are generated in Step 3, never copied:
  ```bash
  cd portable_agent_kit
  mkdir -p /path/to/target/.agents
  cp -r GUIDELINES.md scripts knowledge /path/to/target/
  cp -r .agents/rules .agents/skills /path/to/target/.agents/
  ```
  Do **not** copy `tests/`, `.github/` or `.agents/task_ledger.json` (AIKit's own); the CLI gates above carry enforcement. Replace copied `knowledge/` documents with your project's, and copy `.agents/rules/readme_quickref.md.template` into your `README.md`, replacing `<FILL` placeholders.

### Step 2: Move Your Own Agent Instructions into Tier 1B
If the target already has instruction files, move project-specific rules into `.agents/rules/domain.md` (max 1,200 chars), then delete the originals. Sync injects the block into every generated file and never overwrites hand-authored files without a generated header (`[PROTECTED]`).

### Step 3: Run Principle Synchronization
Generate every Tier 1 file from `GUIDELINES.md`:

```bash
python scripts/sync_principles.py
```
This writes all 8 Tier 1 files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.windsurfrules`, `.clinerules`, `.agents/rules/principles.md`), each <=1,600 tokens including Tier 1B.

### Step 4: Generate Your Knowledge Base
Run the knowledge base AST scanner to automatically index your project's classes and functions:

```bash
python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py
```
This generates `knowledge/codebase_map.md` with every exported class, method, argument, and docstring.

## 🏛️ The 20 Core Principles (Lifecycle-Ordered)

The principles are strictly organized across **5 chronological execution phases**:

<!-- principles:begin (generated from GUIDELINES.md by scripts/sync_principles.py; do not edit) -->
### 🏛️ Phase 1: Meta-Governance & Attentional Grounding
| Principle | Title | Capsule |
|---|---|---|
| **PRINCIPLE-000** | Meta-Principle Integrity & Mutual Alignment | Every rule binds; conflicts follow R6 order; rule edits re-check every citing principle; gaming a gate is a violation; quality doubts go to the user. |
| **PRINCIPLE-001** | Progressive Rule Disclosure & Governance Frugality | Pre-Flight checklist before the first Track C edit; Post-Flight checklist before any Track B or C commit; report only failed items (R8). |
| **PRINCIPLE-002** | Lifecycle-Aligned Instruction Ordering & Attentional Priming | Track via `disruption_recovery.py --track` (A none, B docs/comments but not rule files, C rest); urgency alone never skips P018 gates (R5). |
| **PRINCIPLE-003** | Empirical Grounding & Anti-Hallucination Invariant | Read-before-write slice freshness; `git grep -w -e` call-site check; deps only if declared; platform parity; ask on intent ambiguity; strict AST syntax gate. |
| **PRINCIPLE-004** | Attentional Drift Prevention & Compaction Resilience | Plan = latest `[1/` Phase 2 `--desc` in `task_ledger.json`; cold start `--resume`; never re-ask recorded answers; ADR before commit; reads/output <=100 lines. |

| **PRINCIPLE-006** | Incremental Progress Checkpointing & Disruption Recovery | Commit each `[milestone N/M]` once Phase 4 passes; failing work stays uncommitted, described by `--checkpoint`; `--complete` or `--reset` before switching tasks; `--clean` stale `.tmp_*`. |
| **PRINCIPLE-007** | Pre-flight Impact & Quality Checklist | Track C first plan checkpoint carries --why --benefits --risks (contract, dependency, concurrency, state) --mitigation; no TODO or stub; no change outside the plan. |
| **PRINCIPLE-008** | Hierarchical Problem & Task Decomposition | Plan of M<=6 milestones (more: split into tasks), built bottom-up, each passing Phase 4 alone; re-plan = new `[1/M']` checkpoint; sub-agents never write the ledger. |

### 🏗️ Phase 3: Architecture & Lean Implementation
| Principle | Title | Capsule |
|---|---|---|
| **PRINCIPLE-009** | Modularity & Pluggable Architecture | Every module: no junk-drawer name, roles of 1-5 methods, no import cycle (gated). At a pluggable boundary: 4 layers, registry lookup, constructor DI with default, frozen DTOs. |
| **PRINCIPLE-010** | Performance & Resource Optimization | Stream uncontrolled input; threads only for steps >=200ms; timeout= on subprocess, with on open(); one fsync per file; `--help` <200ms; unit <=8ms, integ <=200ms/test. |
| **PRINCIPLE-011** | Zero-Friction Onboarding & Instant Usability | Only declared deps; creates its dirs; prompts only with `--interactive`; no `os.environ[...]` reads; exit 0/1/2; errors give `Why:`/`Fix:`; demo <10s; other software: its `aikit.py` project is the workspace (R8). |

## ⚡ Disruption Recovery & Power-Loss Protection

If electricity cuts out, battery dies, or the computer crashes mid-task:
1. **Pre-flight Audit**: On a cold start, run this one command first (PRINCIPLE-004 R2):
   ```bash
   python scripts/disruption_recovery.py --resume
   ```
   It prints every `--audit` finding, then the interrupted task, its plan and the phase to resume at. With no interrupted task it says "Ready" only when no uncommitted files exist.
2. **Everything else** (`--audit`, `--checkpoint`, `--complete`, `--reset`, `--clean`) is in the command matrix above; a task's first plan checkpoint must carry `--why --benefits --risks --mitigation`.
3. **Atomic File Safety**: state files are written to a temp file, fsynced and renamed (PRINCIPLE-013); a corrupt ledger is moved to `*.corrupt_*` and restored from its `.bak`.

## 🛠️ Adding New Principles to Your Project

## 🚀 Start a Project

Open this folder in any AI host and describe what to build. Each project gets its own folder under `projects/` (ignored by AIKit's git) and its own git repository; AIKit's gates, map and ledger never read it.

```bash
python aikit.py new my-app          # projects/my-app/: new git repo + .aikit/ memory
python aikit.py attach ../existing  # register a folder elsewhere; adds only .aikit/ and .gitignore lines
python aikit.py list                # every project, its stack and test command
python aikit.py status my-app       # its task, open changes, last decision
python aikit.py check my-app        # its tests, configured checks, hygiene, guidelines, secrets
python aikit.py check my-app --strict  # delivery: clean tree + map
python aikit.py fix my-app          # restore memory/README, refresh map, then check
python aikit.py guideline my-app "money is integer cents" --source user  # project rule
python aikit.py publish my-app      # own private GitHub repo, scanned first
```
A project's memory is its `.aikit/` folder (record, ledger, decisions, guidelines: its own rules, below the principles), committed in its repository; ledger commands take `--workspace projects/<name>`. Stack and test command are detected from its files (Python, Node, Rust, Go, Java, .NET); `--test "<cmd>"` overrides. `check` asks you to record `checklists: passed` or the failed IDs in the task's latest checkpoint before the commit (PRINCIPLE-001 R8, PRINCIPLE-011 R8); a deliberate hygiene finding needs `hygiene: allow <reason>` on its own line.

## 📥 Alternative: Copy AIKit Into an Existing Project

### Step 1: Copy Governance Assets

- Copy the source of truth and tooling; Tier 1 files are generated in Step 3, never copied:
  ```bash
  cd portable_agent_kit
  mkdir -p /path/to/target/.agents
  cp -r GUIDELINES.md scripts knowledge /path/to/target/
  cp -r .agents/rules .agents/skills /path/to/target/.agents/
  ```
  Do **not** copy `tests/`, `.github/` or `.agents/task_ledger.json` (AIKit's own); the CLI gates above carry enforcement. Replace copied `knowledge/` documents with your project's, and copy `.agents/rules/readme_quickref.md.template` into your `README.md`, replacing `<FILL` placeholders.

### Step 2: Move Your Own Agent Instructions into Tier 1B
If the target already has instruction files, move project-specific rules into `.agents/rules/domain.md` (max 1,200 chars), then delete the originals. Sync injects the block into every generated file and never overwrites hand-authored files without a generated header (`[PROTECTED]`).

### Step 3: Run Principle Synchronization
Generate every Tier 1 file from `GUIDELINES.md`:

```bash
python scripts/sync_principles.py
```
This writes all 8 Tier 1 files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.windsurfrules`, `.clinerules`, `.agents/rules/principles.md`), each <=1,600 tokens including Tier 1B.

### Step 4: Generate Your Knowledge Base
Run the knowledge base AST scanner to automatically index your project's classes and functions:

```bash
python scripts/update_knowledge_base.py
```
This generates `knowledge/codebase_map.md` with every exported class, method, argument, and docstring.

## 🏛️ The 20 Core Principles (Lifecycle-Ordered)

The principles are strictly organized across **5 chronological execution phases**:

### 🏛️ Phase 1: Meta-Governance & Attentional Grounding
| Principle | Title | Capsule |
|---|---|---|
| **PRINCIPLE-000** | Meta-Principle Integrity & Mutual Alignment | Every rule binds; conflicts follow R6 order; rule edits re-check every citing principle; gaming a gate is a violation; quality doubts go to the user. |
| **PRINCIPLE-001** | Progressive Rule Disclosure & Governance Frugality | Pre-Flight checklist before the first Track C edit; Post-Flight checklist before any Track B or C commit; report only failed items (R8). |
| **PRINCIPLE-002** | Lifecycle-Aligned Instruction Ordering & Attentional Priming | Track via `disruption_recovery.py --track` (A none, B docs/comments but not rule files, C rest); urgency alone never skips P018 gates (R5). |
| **PRINCIPLE-003** | Empirical Grounding & Anti-Hallucination Invariant | Read-before-write slice freshness; `git grep -w -e` call-site check; deps only if declared; platform parity; ask on intent ambiguity; strict AST syntax gate. |
| **PRINCIPLE-004** | Attentional Drift Prevention & Compaction Resilience | Plan = latest `[1/` Phase 2 `--desc` in `task_ledger.json`; cold start `--resume`; never re-ask recorded answers; ADR before commit; reads/output <=100 lines. |

### 🧭 Phase 2: Pre-Flight Orientation & Planning
| Principle | Title | Capsule |
|---|---|---|
| **PRINCIPLE-005** | AI Cold-Start Readiness & Living Documentation | README <=20k chars: prerequisites, test command, tree; user-visible changes update it same commit; `update_knowledge_base.py --check` gates it. |
| **PRINCIPLE-006** | Incremental Progress Checkpointing & Disruption Recovery | Commit each `[milestone N/M]` once Phase 4 passes; failing work stays uncommitted, described by `--checkpoint`; `--complete` or `--reset` before switching tasks; `--clean` stale `.tmp_*`. |
| **PRINCIPLE-007** | Pre-flight Impact & Quality Checklist | Track C first plan checkpoint carries --why --benefits --risks (contract, dependency, concurrency, state) --mitigation; no TODO or stub; no change outside the plan. |
| **PRINCIPLE-008** | Hierarchical Problem & Task Decomposition | Plan of M<=6 milestones (more: split into tasks), built bottom-up, each passing Phase 4 alone; re-plan = new `[1/M']` checkpoint; sub-agents never write the ledger. |

### 🏗️ Phase 3: Architecture & Lean Implementation
| Principle | Title | Capsule |
|---|---|---|
| **PRINCIPLE-009** | Modularity & Pluggable Architecture | Every module: no junk-drawer name, roles of 1-5 methods, no import cycle (gated). At a pluggable boundary: 4 layers, registry lookup, constructor DI with default, frozen DTOs. |
| **PRINCIPLE-010** | Performance & Resource Optimization | Stream uncontrolled input; threads only for steps >=200ms; timeout= on subprocess, with on open(); one fsync per file; `--help` <200ms; unit <=8ms, integ <=200ms/test. |
| **PRINCIPLE-011** | Zero-Friction Onboarding & Instant Usability | Only declared deps; creates its dirs; prompts only with `--interactive`; no `os.environ[...]` reads; exit 0/1/2; errors give `Why:`/`Fix:`; demo <10s; other software: its `aikit.py` project is the workspace (R8). |
| **PRINCIPLE-012** | Token Frugality & Lean Code Architecture | LLM code: <=16k-char payloads, static prefix first, schema-checked replies, 429 backoff, step caps; agent: diff -U3, search <=50 hits, relative paths. |

| Principle | Title | Capsule |
|---|---|---|
| **PRINCIPLE-013** | Crash Resilience, State Atomicity & Power-Loss Recovery | State files: >=10MB free, temp + fsync + os.replace (5 tries) + dir fsync, .bak, advisory locking 3s/30s stale, corrupt -> quarantine/.bak/migrate. Generated: temp + fsync + replace. |
| **PRINCIPLE-014** | Automated Test Verification & Continuous Test Coverage | 100% test pass gate; behaviour change = failing-first test; weakening a test needs user approval + ADR naming it; unit <=8ms/test, no spawns/sleeps; integ <=200ms/test; tempdir + addCleanup; `scripts/check_reachability.py`. |
| **PRINCIPLE-015** | Universal Operational Dogfooding & Chaos Verification | Domain-specific interactive dogfooding via `scripts/dogfood.py` as a commit gate; golden path + chaos perturbation; non-interactive stdin parity; portable RAII process tree teardown; ephemeral safety jail; terse reporting (<=15 lines). |

| Principle | Title | Capsule |
|---|---|---|
| **PRINCIPLE-016** | AI Knowledge Base & Continuous Synchronization | Canonical `knowledge/` sync; atomic code-and-doc pairing; monotonic append-only ADR register; strict AST syntax validation; link integrity shield; `scripts/update_knowledge_base.py`. |

If electricity cuts out, battery dies, or the computer crashes mid-task:

the integration tier has a 3.49s floor from 35 real CLI spawns. An absolute
per-suite cap also breaks whenever a correct, fast test is added, which
pressures an agent to delete coverage instead.

Both budgets are now per-test averages, 8ms for the unit tier and 200ms for
the integration tier, with 37% and 13% headroom over the slowest measured
run. `scripts/check_test_budgets.py` runs each tier once, reads the count and
duration unittest prints, and fails when a tier fails, when its output
carries no summary, or when its average exceeds the ceiling. PRINCIPLE-018 R3
item (1) names it, so Phase 4 runs the tiers through it rather than twice.

The user approved this relaxation; ADR-144 records it and, under
